ashley: heads-up — saw a weird pattern in overnight bench: A100 p99 spikes when we fall back to the non-optimized kernel at tiny batch sizes. can someone sanity-check? :thinking:
kenji: ugh OK. which config + model?
ashley: quick repro used gpt-3small (dense), batch=1, seq=512, kv-cache enabled, quant=fp16, driver 535.11.03. saw p50 ~40ms but p99 ~420ms on A100, H100 looks stable ~80ms p99. tested L40S too and it's noisy but not as bad as A100.
sam: can you paste the bench command and output?
ashley: sure — run I used:
```
./run_bench --model=gpt-3small --gpus=A100,H100,L40S --batch=1 --seq=512 --kv-cache=on --quant=fp16 --iters=500 --warmup=50
```
benchbot: ran the above overnight on pool-2. summary (median / p99 in ms):
```
A100  median=38  p99=420  notes="fallbacks: 7%
CPU steal small spikes"
H100  median=36  p99=82   notes="fallbacks: 0.3%"
L40S  median=45  p99=150  notes="fallbacks: 2%"
```
kenji: that 7% fallback rate is suspicious. looks like kernel selection failing for some sequence lengths. can you check if those p99s align with GPU power/thermal logs?
maria: also check NVLINK/PCIe utilization. if a100 instances had cross-node traffic or noisy-neighbor vGPU, that could blow up p99. which instance type?
ashley: these were dedicated A100-sXM4-40GB (single card), no vGPU. attached the perf sample ID 20260301-ascend-09 (link to dashboard).
daryl: another guess: the fallback might be triggered by small scratchpad allocation failing under fragmentation — we saw this with 535 drivers and older CUDA. any recent kernel patches?
kenji: good point. can you try forcing the optimized kernel flag off/on and re-run short sweep? i.e. force_kernel=optimized vs force_kernel=compat and compare fallback counts.
ashley: doing that now — kicking off 3 quick runs (force=opt, force=compat, force=auto) each 200 iters, seq=512. will post results.
benchbot: started jobs: run-1745554321-1 (A100 force=opt), run-1745554321-2 (A100 force=compat), run-1745554321-3 (H100 force=auto). ETA ~8m.
sam: if the A100 only shows spikes with force=opt then maybe a kernel bug that trips on some inputs. if force=compat reduces throughput but stabilizes latency, that's actionable for rollout.
maria: also capture nv-memcheck / CUCI logs on the failing window and collect `nvidia-smi dmon` 1s. we need correlating counters.
ashley: results in — run-1 (force=opt): median=36 p99=410 fallback=6.8%
run-2 (force=compat): median=44 p99=92 fallback=0.2%
run-3 (H100 auto): median=35 p99=80 fallback=0.4%
kenji: confirms it. optimized kernel giving best median but causes sporadic fallbacks with huge p99 on A100. compatibility kernel trades latency for stability.
daryl: next step: reduce fallback surface by increasing scratchpad reservation for the kernel path. cc @sam to check whether we can bump allocation heuristics in runtime.
sam: yes I can prototype a conservative reservation for small-batch long-seq combos. i'll spin a branch with a flag `reserve_scratch_for_small_batch=true` and run internal smoke.
maria: meanwhile, can we gate A100 auto-rollout in prod for this model? we should prefer compat kernel until we get fix. ops/traffic team needs heads up.
ashley: filing a quick PRD and rollout note. also adding a perf regression alert for fallback_rate > 1% on A100 for any model.
kenji: +1. please include the benchmark command and attach the `nvidia-smi` trace. i can take a look at the kernel selection logs and open a driver ticket if needed.
benchbot: job run-1745554321-1 logs: link to s3://redwood-bench/1745554321/run-1/logs.txt
benchbot: job run-1745554321-2 logs: link to s3://redwood-bench/1745554321/run-2/logs.txt
ashley: thanks all. i'll coordinate with ops to freeze A100 auto for gpt-3small and post the PRD in #eng-release. will follow up once sam's branch has smoke results. :thumbsup:
kenji: thanks ashley — if you hit anything weird ping me and i'll triage kernel traces. :eyes:
